abstract_en: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. Sotatercept, an activin-signaling inhibitor, is a novel therapy targeting this pathology. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess its efficacy and safety in PAH. A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating Sotatercept in adults with PAH. Data were pooled using random-effects models to estimate mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Four RCTs enrolling 921 patients were included. Compared with placebo, Sotatercept significantly improved 6-minute walk distance (MD 30.54 m, 95% CI 4.05-57.04, P=0.02), WHO functional class (RR 1.71, 95% CI 1.37-2.15, P<0.00001), multicomponent improvement (RR 2.77, 95% CI 1.45-5.29, P=0.002), pulmonary vascular resistance (MD -197.01 dyn⋅s⋅cm-5, 95% CI -213.16 - -180.86, P<0.00001), and reduced clinical worsening events (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.21-0.38, P<0.00001). There were no significant differences in NT-proBNP levels or all-cause mortality. Safety analysis showed lower risks of serious adverse events (AEs), peripheral edema, and right ventricular failure, but higher rates of bleeding, epistaxis, and drug-related AEs. Sotatercept demonstrated meaningful clinical benefits in exercise capacity, hemodynamics, and disease progression among patients with PAH, with a generally acceptable safety profile. These findings support Sotatercept as a promising adjunct to standard therapy, though longer-term trials are needed to confirm durability and survival impact.
abstract_es: Abstract

La hipertensión arterial pulmonar (HAP) es una enfermedad progresiva caracterizada por remodelación vascular pulmonar y aumento de la resistencia vascular pulmonar. Sotatercept, un inhibidor de la señalización de la activina, es una terapia novedosa dirigida a esta patología. Realizamos una revisión sistemática y metaanálisis para evaluar su eficacia y seguridad en la HAP. Se realizó una búsqueda sistemática de PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Escopus y Web of Science para identificar ensayos controlados aleatorios (RCT) que evaluaron Sotatercept en adultos con HAP. Los datos fueron agrupados utilizando modelos de efectos aleatorios para estimar diferencias medias (MDs) y ratios de riesgo (RRs) con intervalos de confianza del 95% (ICs). En comparación con placebo, Sotatercept mejoró significativamente la distancia a pie de 6 minutos (MD 30,54 m, IC 95% 4,05-57,04, P=0,02), clase funcional de la OMS (RR 1,71, IC 95% 1,37-2,15, P<0,00001), mejoría multicomponente (RR 2,77, IC 95% 1,45-5,29, P=0,002), resistencia vascular pulmonar (MD -197,01 dyns­zcm-5, IC 95% -213,16 - -180,86, P<0,00001) y empeoramiento clínico reducido (RR 0,28, IC 95% 0,21-0,38, P<0,00001). No hubo diferencias significativas en los niveles de NT-proBNP o mortalidad por cualquier causa. El análisis de seguridad mostró menores riesgos de eventos adversos graves (AE), edema periférico e insuficiencia ventricular derecha, pero mayores tasas de sangrado, epistaxis y EA relacionados con el fármaco. Sotatercept demostró beneficios clínicos significativos en la capacidad de ejercicio, hemodinámica y progresión de la enfermedad entre los pacientes con HAP, con un perfil de seguridad generalmente aceptable. Estos hallazgos apoyan a Sotatercept como un complemento prometedor a la terapia estándar, aunque se necesitan ensayos a más largo plazo para confirmar la durabilidad y el impacto en la supervivencia.

abstract_en:
Background
Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction being the cornerstone of prevention. Despite effective therapies, many high-risk patients do not achieve recommended LDL-C targets. Enlicitide (MK-0616), an oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, offers a potential alternative to injectable PCSK9-directed therapies.Objective
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of enlicitide in adults with hypercholesterolemia and assess its dose-dependent effects on lipid parameters.Methods
We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through March 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood estimation was performed. The primary outcome was the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline. Secondary outcomes included non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), lipoprotein(a), triglycerides, and safety outcomes. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2.0 and GRADE.Results
Three placebo-controlled RCTs involving 3593 participants were included. Enlicitide significantly reduced LDL-C compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], -56.19%; 95% CI, -64.14 to -48.25; p 2 = 56.9%). Significant reductions were also observed in non-HDL-C (MD, -51.36%), ApoB (MD, -47.09%), lipoprotein(a) (MD, -20.10%), and triglycerides (MD, -13.12%). A numerical dose-response gradient was observed, although subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and treatment discontinuation were comparable between groups.Conclusion
Enlicitide produced substantial reductions in LDL-C and other atherogenic lipid parameters without an apparent increase in adverse events. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of trials, moderate heterogeneity, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. Dose-response, duration-related lipoprotein(a), and triglyceride findings were exploratory and substantially driven by single trials. Long-term cardiovascular outcomes trials are needed to establish clinical benefit.

Introduction
Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU.Methods
PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Safety outcomes included mortality, urinary tract infection, upper respiratory tract infection, injection-site reactions, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Adalimumab provides the most consistent evidence for reducing treatment failure in NIU. Comparative safety estimates, particularly for infliximab, remain uncertain and hypothesis-generating. Larger, long-term, head-to-head trials are required.

abstract_en: Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a major contributor to global mortality and long-term cardiovascular risk despite optimal treatment. Colchicine, an anti-inflammatory agent, has gained attention for its potential benefits in ACS. This meta-analysis evaluates its safety and impact on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) levels, and cardiac function in ACS patients. Methods: We performed a systematic literature search of randomized controlled trials on PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus databases from inception to January 1st, 2025. We pooled dichotomous outcomes as risk ratios (RR) and continuous outcomes as mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals, using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and X2 statistics. Statistical significance was defined by a p-value Results: The meta-analysis included 18 RCTs involving 14,688 patients (7,336 receiving colchicine and 7,352 controls). 11,742 (79.94%) were men and mean age was 59.8±8.8 years. Compared to placebo, colchicine reduced the rate of MACE (RR=0.74, 95%CI:0.60 to 0.92), even when examined after 1 or more years of therapy (RR 0.83, 95%CI:0.70 to 0.98), reduced hsCRP levels (MD -0.80, 95%CI:-1.34 to -0.27), and improved left ventricular ejection fraction (MD 1.13, 95%CI:0.25 to 2.02]). While no increase in overall adverse events was seen with colchicine (RR 1.00, 95% CI: 0.95 to 1.06), diarrhea occurred more frequently (RR=1.52, 95%CI: 1.03 to 2.24). Conclusion: Colchicine appears safe and may improve long-term outcomes in ACS patients. However, larger studies with more extended follow-up are needed for definitive evidence.

abstract_en: Iron deficiency affects approximately half of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and impairs functional capacity, yet evidence for intravenous (IV) iron in this population is limited. We evaluated the effect of IV iron on functional, biochemical, biomarker, and clinical outcomes in HFpEF. This systematic review followed PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 and was prospectively registered [International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) CRD420261360828]. Four databases were searched on April 11, 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adults with HFpEF and iron deficiency receiving IV iron, with at least 4 weeks of follow-up. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Because few studies were eligible and heterogeneity was substantial, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis in accordance with the synthesis without meta-analysis guideline, and certainty was rated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework. Seven reports of 6 studies were included: 1 randomized trial, 2 controlled observational studies, and 3 single-arm before-after studies. Across studies, IV iron consistently increased ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hemoglobin. The randomized trial improved 6-minute walking distance but not functional class or quality of life, and was stopped early. Effects on natriuretic peptide concentrations were inconsistent. The 2 controlled studies disagreed on clinical events: a propensity-matched analysis reported fewer hospitalizations, whereas a registry found no benefit. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. In HFpEF, IV iron reliably corrects iron indices, but a clinical benefit remains unproven, and the evidence base is sparse and largely uncontrolled. Adequately powered randomized trials are required.

abstract_en: Conduction system pacing (CSP) is an emerging alternative to biventricular pacing (BVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have yielded divergent results, creating uncertainty about the comparative effectiveness. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs comparing CSP with BVP for CRT, searching PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through May 2026 (updating a prior review). The primary outcome was change in left ventricular ejection fraction (ΔLVEF), analyzed with random-effects models and prediction intervals. Eight parallel-group RCTs including 799 patients (396 CSP, 403 BVP) were included. Pooled ΔLVEF did not differ significantly (MD +2.40%, 95% CI -0.49 to 5.29, p = 0.091; I2 = 75%). CSP showed a non-significant trend toward shorter paced QRS (MD -7.6 ms, p = 0.14) and improved NYHA class (SMD -0.33, p = 0.12). Heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.69), mortality (RR 1.17), complications (RR 0.84), and procedure time did not differ. The four trials enrolling exclusively LBBB patients favored CSP (MD +5.00%, 95% CI 3.01 to 6.98, p = 0.004; I2 = 0%), consistent in the three using confirmed LBBAP/LBBP (MD +5.37%, 95% CI 3.23 to 7.52, p = 0.008; I2 = 0%). Because no non-inferiority margin was prespecified and the clinical-event analyses were underpowered, these findings should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence or comparable safety. Exploratory analyses suggest that patients with LBBB undergoing LBBAP/LBBP may derive incremental benefit, warranting confirmation in adequately powered trials.

abstract_en: Conduction system pacing (CSP) has emerged as a promising modality for cardiac resynchronization therapy, but evidence of CSP in heart failure (HF) remains controversial. The authors aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of CSP, including left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) and His bundle pacing, to biventricular pacing (BiVP) in HF. The MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL databases were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) and all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included clinical endpoints (HHF, all-cause mortality), cardiac resynchronization therapy responses (predefined and super-response), echocardiographic parameters (left ventricular ejection fraction and left ventricular end-systolic volume), electrophysiologic parameters (paced QRS duration and capture threshold), functional status (NYHA functional class and 6-minute walk test distance), procedural performance (procedural time, fluoroscopy time, lead implantation time), and device-related complications. (PROSPERO registration: CRD420261388077). Twelve randomized controlled trials involving 1,054 patients (566 CSP and 488 BiVP) were included. CSP showed a significant reduction in primary composite endpoint (OR: 0.30; 95% CI: 0.18-0.52; I2 = 0%), improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (mean difference: 3.06%; 95% CI: 0.82%-5.30%; I2 = 55%), and shorter paced QRS duration (mean difference:-11.49 ms; 95% CI: -20.70 to -2.28; I2 = 85%), compared with BiVP. In the LBBAP group, there were greater reductions in primary composite endpoint with higher rates of super-response (OR: 2.18; 95% CI: 1.44-3.30; I2 = 54%) compared with BiVP. No differences were observed in functional status or device-related complications. CSP, and potentially LBBAP, was associated with a significantly lower composite endpoint of HHF and all-cause mortality compared with BiVP, supporting CSP as an alternative to BiVP in HF.

No se observaron diferencias en el estado funcional o complicaciones relacionadas con el dispositivo. abstract_en: IntroductionSystemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and lupus nephritis (LN) carry substantial cardiorenal risks. Conventional immunosuppressive therapies primarily target inflammation but leave a burden of residual renal and metabolic damage. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide clear cardiorenal protection in general populations, but data specific to SLE remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of SGLT2i in patients with SLE and LN.MethodsComprehensive searches across five electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus) were conducted up to April 2026 to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies assessing SGLT2i in adult SLE/LN patients. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize cardiorenal and safety outcomes using R Software.ResultsSix studies published between 2024 and 2025 were included. Pooled data demonstrated that SGLT2i use was associated with a significant improvement in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) compared to controls (MD: 4.02; 95% CI: 1.39-6.65; I2 = 60.1%). SGLT2i significantly reduced the risks of progression to end-stage kidney disease (RR: 0.37; 95% CI: 0.25-0.56; I2 = 11.0%), heart failure development (RR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.56-0.75; I2 = 0.0%), incident lupus nephritis (RR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.44-0.76; I2 = 0.0%), and re-hospitalizations (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.57-0.79; I2 = 0.0%). Furthermore, a significant reduction in all-cause mortality was observed (RR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.36-0.86; I2 = 76.2%). SGLT2i treatment demonstrated an acceptable safety profile across the included cohorts. The certainty of evidence for these findings was rated as low to very low, and results remain vulnerable to residual confounding from variables such as disease activity, corticosteroid burden, and immunosuppressive regimen.ConclusionPreliminary exploratory evidence suggests potential associations between SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiorenal outcomes in lupus nephritis. Given the low certainty of evidence and vulnerability to residual confounding from disease-specific variables, these hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in well-designed randomized controlled trials.

abstract_en: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain. We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials. We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding. Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies. Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

El manejo óptimo de la enfermedad arterial coronaria en pacientes con estenosis aórtica grave sometidos a implante valvular aórtico transcatéter (TAVI) sigue siendo incierto, con el objetivo de comparar los resultados clínicos entre la revascularización coronaria rutinaria y el manejo conservador en pacientes sometidos a TAVI y evaluar la eficacia relativa de las estrategias de revascularización individuales mediante la realización de un metaanálisis de ensayos aleatorizados. Se realizó un metaanálisis de pares comparando la intervención coronaria percutánea (ICP) con el tratamiento conservador y un metaanálisis de red comparando la efectividad relativa de estrategias individuales, incluyendo ICP guiada por angiografía y fisiología. El resultado primario fue una variable compuesta definida en el estudio de eventos cardiovasculares adversos mayores (MACE). Los criterios secundarios incluyeron los resultados individuales de muerte por todas las causas, muerte cardiovascular, infarto de miocardio, accidente cerebrovascular, revascularización no planificada y hemorragia mayor. Cinco ensayos (N=1.644 pacientes) fueron incluidos en la revisión sistemática, y cuatro fueron incluidos en la síntesis cuantitativa primaria (N=1.476). En comparación con el tratamiento conservador, la ICP de rutina se asoció con menores riesgos de MACE (cociente de riesgo [RR] 0,80, intervalo de confianza del 95% [IC]: 0,65-0,98) y revascularización no planificada (RR 0,30, IC 95%: 0,11-0,83) y un aumento del riesgo de hemorragia mayor (RR 1,57, IC 95%: 1,07-2,32). En el metaanálisis de red, la ICP guiada por fisiología redujo significativamente el MACE, el ictus y la revascularización no planificada en comparación con el tratamiento conservador y ubicó los resultados isquémicos más altos entre las estrategias de revascularización. En este contexto, la ICP guiada por fisiología puede estar asociada con el perfil de eficacia más favorable en todas las estrategias disponibles. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

abstract_en: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) is a major cause of chronic heart failure with impaired left ventricular (LV) function. Trimetazidine, a metabolic modulator that shifts energy utilization from fatty acid oxidation to glucose oxidation, may improve cardiac function in ischemic myocardium. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate trimetazidine's effect in patients with ICM compared to standard therapy alone. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, ProQuest, SAGE, EBSCO Host, Wiley, Science Direct, and SpringerLink databases until November 2024. Clinical trials assessing trimetazidine versus standard therapy in ICM were included. Data were analyzed using a random-effects model to calculate mean differences (MD) and relative risk (RR), with heterogeneity evaluated using the I2 statistic. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria. Trimetazidine significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (MD 6.35%, 95% CI: 4.63-8.07; p<0.05), reduced LV end-systolic diameter (MD -4.51 mm, p<0.05), LV end-diastolic diameter (MD -3.13 mm, p<0.05), and LV end-systolic volume (MD -14.20 ml, p<0.05). Exercise capacity improved markedly with a mean increase of 83.64 meters in the 6-minute walking test (p<0.05). NYHA class also improved (MD -0.80, p<0.05). However, no significant differences were found in anginal episodes or nitrate consumption. Trimetazidine as an adjunct to standard therapy improves cardiac function and exercise capacity in ischemic cardiomyopathy patients. It may be considered in patients with persistent symptoms or exercise intolerance despite optimal medical therapy. Further large-scale trials are warranted to assess long-term outcomes such as mortality and hospitalization.
abstract_es: Abstract

La cardiomiopatía isquémica (ICM) es una causa importante de insuficiencia cardíaca crónica con función del ventrículo izquierdo (VI) alterada. La trimetazidina, un modulador metabólico que cambia la utilización de energía de la oxidación de ácidos grasos a la oxidación de glucosa, puede mejorar la función cardíaca en el miocardio isquémico. Este metaanálisis tuvo como objetivo evaluar el efecto de la trimetazidina en pacientes con MIC en comparación con el tratamiento estándar solo. Se realizó una búsqueda sistemática a través de las bases de datos PubMed, ProQuest, SAGE, EBSCO Host, Wiley, Science Direct y SpringerLink hasta noviembre de 2024. Los datos fueron analizados utilizando un modelo de efectos aleatorios para calcular las diferencias medias (MD) y el riesgo relativo (RR), con la heterogeneidad evaluada utilizando el estadístico I2. Diez estudios cumplieron los criterios de inclusión. Trimetazidina mejoró significativamente la fracción de eyección del ventrículo izquierdo (MD 6,35%, IC 95%: 4,63-8,07; p<0,05), redujo el diámetro sistólico final del VI (MD -4,51 mm, p<0,05), el diámetro diastólico final del VI (MD -3,13 mm, p<0,05) y el volumen sistólico final del VI (MD -14,20 ml, p<0,05). La capacidad de ejercicio mejoró notablemente con un aumento medio de 83,64 metros en la prueba de caminar de 6 minutos (p<0,05). La clase NYHA también mejoró (MD -0,80, p<0,05). Sin embargo, no se encontraron diferencias significativas en episodios anginales o consumo de nitratos. La trimetazidina como complemento a la terapia estándar mejora la función cardíaca y la capacidad de ejercicio en pacientes con cardiomiopatía isquémica. Se puede considerar en pacientes con síntomas persistentes o intolerancia al ejercicio a pesar de una terapia médica óptima.

abstract_en:
Background
Permanent pacemaker implantation is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Leadless pacemakers (LPs) may reduce lead- and pocket-related complications, but their clinical outcomes after TAVR remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety and effectiveness of LPs compared with transvenous pacemakers (TVPs).Methods
PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized and observational studies were included. abstract_en: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents the interconnected pathophysiology of metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and cardiovascular disease, leading to multiorgan dysfunction and elevated adverse outcomes. Overactivation of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), via aldosterone-dependent and ligand-independent pathways, drives inflammation, fibrosis, and oxidative stress and facilitates CKM progression. Finerenone is a selective non-steroidal MR antagonist (nsMRA) that exhibits high MR affinity, has balanced cardiac and renal distribution, and minimal off-target steroidal effects, which make it mechanistically different from steroidal MRAs. Large phase 3 trials such as FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD in type 2 diabetes with CKD, and FINEARTS-HF in heart failure (HF) with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) > 40%, demonstrated consistent cardiorenal benefits. The prespecified FINE-HEART pooled analysis showed finerenone reduced all-cause mortality (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.99), HF hospitalizations (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.75-0.92), and the kidney composite outcome (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90), with benefits consistent across CKM components and background therapies including sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. Recent data from FIND-CKD extend utility to non-diabetic CKD. Various guidelines incorporate finerenone as an additive therapy for patients with persistent albuminuria on maximal renin-angiotensin system inhibition (RASi) + SGLT2i. This review summarizes the MR pathophysiology in CKM syndrome, compares the mechanisms of non-steroidal versus steroidal MRAs, synthesizes clinical trial evidence, safety, and guideline-directed place in therapy, addresses implementation barriers, including cost, and outlines future research directions. Finerenone may fill a critical gap in multimodal CKM management, enabling comprehensive pillar-based therapy to mitigate residual cardiorenal risk.

El síndrome cardiovascular-quidney-metabólico (CKM) representa la fisiopatología interconectada de factores de riesgo metabólicos, enfermedad renal crónica (CKD) y enfermedad cardiovascular, lo que conduce a disfunción multiorgánica y resultados adversos elevados. La sobreactivación del receptor mineralocorticoide (MR), a través de vías dependientes de aldosterona e independientes de ligando, impulsa inflamación, fibrosis y estrés oxidativo y facilita la progresión de la CKM. La finenona es un antagonista selectivo de la RM no esteroidea (nsMRA) que exhibe una alta afinidad por la RM, tiene una distribución cardíaca y renal equilibrada y efectos esteroidales mínimos fuera de la meta, que lo hacen mecánicamente diferente de los MRA esteroideos. Los ensayos en fase 3 grandes, como FIDELIO-DKD y FIGARO-DKD en diabetes tipo 2 con ERC, y FINEARTS-HF en insuficiencia cardiaca (HF) con fracción de eyección ventricular izquierda (FEVI) > 40%, demostraron beneficios cardiorrenales consistentes. El análisis agrupado preespecificado de FINE-HEART mostró que la finrenona redujo la mortalidad por todas las causas (HR 0,91, IC 95% 0,84-0,99), hospitalizaciones por IC (HR 0,83, IC 95% 0,75-0,92) y el resultado compuesto renal (HR 0,80, IC 95% 0,72-0,90), con beneficios consistentes entre los componentes de la MKC y las terapias de fondo, incluyendo inhibidores del cotransportador de glucosa de sodio 2 (SGLT2). Varias directrices incorporan la finrenona como terapia aditiva para pacientes con albuminuria persistente sobre inhibición máxima del sistema renina-angiotensina (RASi) + SGLT2i. Esta revisión resume la fisiopatología de la RM en el síndrome de CKM, compara los mecanismos de ARM no esteroideos versus esteroides, sintetiza la evidencia de ensayos clínicos, la seguridad y el lugar orientado a la guía en el tratamiento, aborda las barreras de implementación, incluyendo el costo, y esboza las futuras direcciones de investigación. La finrenona puede llenar un vacío crítico en el manejo multimodal de la CKM, permitiendo una terapia integral basada en pilares para mitigar el riesgo cardiorrenal residual.

abstract_en: Obstructive sleep apnea affects approximately one billion adults worldwide and is associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. Obesity is its dominant reversible cause, yet positive airway pressure therapy splints the pharyngeal airway without addressing the adiposity that narrows it, and randomized trials have not shown that it reduces cardiovascular events. In December 2024, the United States Food and Drug Administration approved tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, as the first drug for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. We summarize the pharmacology of tirzepatide and the anatomic basis by which weight reduction improves upper airway patency, notably reduction of tongue and parapharyngeal fat. We then review the SURMOUNT-OSA program: two parallel 52-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolling 469 adults with obesity and an apnea-hypopnea index of at least 15 events per hour, one conducted without positive airway pressure and one during established positive airway pressure use. abstract_en: Exercise training improves cardiorespiratory fitness in patients with heart failure, yet the dose-response relationship across different exercise modalities remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different exercise modalities and their standardized doses on peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) in patients with heart failure. We systematically searched multiple databases from inception through March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise interventions with controls. Exercise modalities were categorized as interval aerobic training (IAT), continuous aerobic training (CAT), resistance training (RT), mind-body training (MBT), and their combinations. Exercise dose was uniformly quantified as weekly metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week). A Bayesian model-based network dose-response meta-analysis was performed. A total of 100 trials involving 5,353 patients were included. The dose-response relationship followed an Emax curve, with ED50 values clustering around 80-90 MET-min/week. A weekly dose of 500 MET-min yielded considerable benefit, and 750-1000 MET-min approached maximal benefit for nearly all modalities. The top three ranked interventions were IAT (Emax = 3.50, 95% CrI: 2.49-4.60), RT (Emax = 3.66, 95% CrI: 1.96-5.85), and IAT+RT (Emax = 3.49, 95% CrI: 1.26-5.79). The exercise dose-response relationship in heart failure follows an Emax curve, with distinct dose-benefit profiles across different exercise modalities. Based on the current evidence, the following preliminary considerations may be offered: for patients with limited exercise tolerance, MBT may be considered as one of the preferred options; for those with moderate exercise tolerance, IAT+RT or CAT+RT may be suitable choices; for patients with good exercise tolerance, IAT or RT may be considered; and for patients with comorbid obesity, CAT may be incorporated into a comprehensive management program.

abstract_en: Catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence and improves symptoms and quality of life (QoL), but sham-controlled trials have reported discordant results. Ablation improved AFEQT relative to sham by 13.5 points (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.6 to 26.9), with a posterior probability of benefit 0.98, of exceeding the 5-point minimal clinically important difference 0.94, and by 12.9 points (-0.4 to 27.1; probability 0.97 and 0.91) with PVI-SHAM-AF's primary estimator. Ablation reduced AF recurrence in every trial (pooled risk ratio 0.49, CrI 0.17-0.89). Certainty was moderate for AF burden and recurrence and low for QoL. Compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control, catheter ablation reduces AF recurrence and burden and has a high probability of clinically important QoL benefit, although its magnitude remains uncertain. La ablación con catéter reduce la recurrencia de la fibrilación auricular (AF) y mejora los síntomas y la calidad de vida (QoL), pero los ensayos simulados han reportado resultados discordantes. Para sintetizar los ensayos simulados de la ablación con FA e identificar por qué los resultados de la CV difieren. Buscamos bases de datos y registros para ensayos aleatorizados de ablación con catéter versus simulaciones en FA sintomática. El resultado principal fue la diferencia entre grupos en la puntuación del efecto de la fibrilación auricular en la calidad de vida (AFEQT), agrupada utilizando un modelo de efectos aleatorios bayesiano. Cuatro ensayos (468 pacientes) fueron elegibles; tres (448 pacientes) fueron agrupados. La ablación mejoró el AFEQT en relación con el simulacro en 13,5 puntos (intervalo creíble del 95% [CrI] 1,6 a 26.9), con una probabilidad posterior de beneficio 0,98, de superar la diferencia clínicamente importante mínima de 5 puntos 0,94, y en 12,9 puntos (-0,4 a 27,1; probabilidad 0,97 y 0,91) con el estimador primario de PVI-SHAM-AF. La heterogeneidad (8,2 puntos, I2 85,3%) se atribuyó en gran medida a PVI-SHAM-AF, que difería de los otros ensayos en severidad sintomática, monitorización del ritmo y evaluación del cegamiento; sin ella, la diferencia fue de 18,9 puntos (6,7 a 31,4). La ablación redujo la recurrencia de FA en todos los ensayos (coeficiente de riesgo compartido 0.49, CrI 0,17-0.89). La certeza fue moderada para la carga de FA y la recurrencia y baja para la CV. Comparada con la farsa incrustada en el control del ritmo activo, la ablación del catéter reduce la recurrencia y la carga de FA y tiene una alta probabilidad de beneficio de CV clínicamente importante, aunque su magnitud sigue siendo incierta.

Two-sample Mendelian randomization assessed causality, and molecular docking verified binding. Results  The meta-analysis included 7 studies (n = 409). abstract_en: Abstract    Background  Older adults receiving long-term antihypertensive therapy represent a rapidly growing surgical population in whom intraoperative blood pressure management remains contentious. Observational evidence consistently links intraoperative hypotension with adverse postoperative outcomes, but whether specific blood pressure targets or hemodynamic management strategies improve clinical outcomes remains uncertain  Methods  We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov from 1 January 2013 to 15 January 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective or retrospective cohort studies of haemodynamic monitoring-guided management in patients with a mean or median age of at least 65 years receiving chronic antihypertensive therapy or with documented chronic hypertension undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data using a piloted form capturing design, setting, population, hypertension status, intervention, comparator, and raw outcome events, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2 for RCTs; ROBINS-I for cohort studies). Quantitative pooling was prespecified only for comparisons with three or more studies sharing design, intervention class, and outcome definition; otherwise, a structured narrative synthesis with fully tabulated study-level effect data was performed. Certainty was rated with GRADE. Reporting follows PRISMA 2020.  Results  Nineteen studies (7 randomized controlled trials reported in 9 publications; 12 cohort studies) comprising 1,074,313 patients were included. In RCTs, higher or individualized intraoperative blood pressure targets did not reduce major vascular or organ-injury composites compared with routine targets (POISE-3: risk ratio [RR] 0.99, 95% CI 0.89–1.11; IMPROVE-multi: RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.93–1.30), although one small trial favoured individualized systolic targets (INPRESS: RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57–0.95); certainty was low because of inconsistency and indirectness. Observational cohorts consistently reported duration-dependent associations between intraoperative hypotension and acute kidney injury or myocardial injury (moderate certainty for the association, not for a causal effect of any specific target). Goal-directed haemodynamic therapy was neutral in the largest contemporary trial (OPTIMISE II: postoperative infection RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.88–1.18) but beneficial in smaller earlier trials (low certainty). Continuing renin–angiotensin-system inhibitors increased intraoperative hypotension (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.19–1.44) without increasing major complications (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.87–1.19; moderate certainty). A hypotension-avoidance strategy did not reduce postoperative delirium in randomized data (cogPOISE-3: RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.79–1.38), and observational findings were inconsistent (low certainty).  Conclusions  Intraoperative hypotension is consistently and duration-dependently associated with organ injury in observational surgical cohorts, although much of this evidence is derived from broader non-cardiac surgical populations rather than exclusively elderly hypertensive patients. Randomized evidence specific to elderly hypertensive populations remains limited and does not demonstrate consistent benefit from higher blood pressure targets, goal-directed haemodynamic therapy, or specific antihypertensive withholding strategies.Recommendations for this population should rest on guidelines and individualized judgment rather than on claims of moderate-certainty trial evidence that the current literature does not provide. Renal denervation and other device-based therapies are outside the scope of this review and are identified as future research priorities only.

Resumen Antecedentes Los adultos mayores que reciben terapia antihipertensiva a largo plazo representan una población quirúrgica en rápido crecimiento en la que el manejo de la presión arterial intraoperatoria sigue siendo polémico. La evidencia observacional vincula consistentemente la hipotensión intraoperatoria con los resultados postoperatorios adversos, pero si los objetivos específicos de presión arterial o las estrategias de manejo hemodinámico mejoran los resultados clínicos permanecen inciertos Métodos Buscamos PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, el Registro Central de Ensayos Controlados de Cochrane, Web of Science y ClinicalTrials.gov del 1 de enero de 2013 al 15 de enero de 2026 para estudios aleatorizados controlados (RCT) y estudios prospectivos o retrospectivos de cohortes de control hemodinámico guiado en pacientes con una edad media o mediana de 65 años que reciben tratamiento antihipertensivo crónico o con hipertensión crónica documentada en cirugía no cardiaca. Dos revisores revisaron de forma independiente los registros, extrajeron datos utilizando una forma piloto capturando diseño, ajuste, población, estado de hipertensión, intervención, comparador y eventos de resultado bruto, y evaluaron el riesgo de sesgo (RoB 2 para ECA; ROBINS-I para estudios de cohortes). La agrupación cuantitativa fue preespecificada sólo para comparaciones con tres o más estudios compartiendo diseño, clase de intervención y definición de resultado; de lo contrario, se realizó una síntesis narrativa estructurada con datos de efecto completamente tabulados. La certeza fue calificada con GRADE. Resultados Se incluyeron 19 estudios (7 ensayos controlados aleatorizados reportados en 9 publicaciones; 12 estudios de cohortes) que incluyeron 1.074.313 pacientes.En los ECA, los objetivos de presión arterial intraoperatoria mayor o individualizada no redujeron los compuestos vasculares mayores u órganos lesionados en comparación con los objetivos de rutina (POISE-3: relación de riesgo [RR] 0,99, IC 95% 0,89–1,11; IMPROVE-multi: RR 1,10, IC 95% 0,93–1,30), aunque un ensayo pequeño favoreció los objetivos sistólicos individualizados (INPRESS: RR 0,74, IC 95% 0,57–0,95); la certeza fue baja debido a inconsistencia e indirecta. Las cohortes observacionales notificaron de manera consistente asociaciones dependientes de la duración entre hipotensión intraoperatoria y lesión renal aguda o lesión miocárdica (confianza moderada para la asociación, no para un efecto causal de ningún objetivo específico).La terapia hemodinámica dirigida por los objetivos fue neutra en el ensayo contemporáneo más grande (OPTIMISE II: infección postoperatoria RR 1,02; IC 95% 0,88–1,18), pero beneficiosa en ensayos previos más pequeños (con poca certeza). Una estrategia de evitación de la hipotensión no redujo el delirio postoperatorio en los datos aleatorizados (cogPOISE-3: RR 1,04, IC 95% 0,79–1,38), y los hallazgos observacionales fueron inconsistentes (baja certeza). Conclusiones La hipotensión intraoperatoria se asocia de manera consistente y dependiente de la duración con la lesión orgánica en cohortes quirúrgicas observacionales, aunque gran parte de esta evidencia se deriva de poblaciones quirúrgicas no cardiacas más amplias que exclusivamente pacientes hipertensos de edad avanzada. abstract_en:
Objective
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved cancer outcomes, yet cardiovascular toxicities remain difficult to recognize and manage. We review their clinical spectrum, mechanistic evidence, diagnostic work-up, surveillance, and treatment, with particular attention to where evidence is established and where it remains preliminary.Methods
We conducted a narrative review of PubMed through September 2026 and hand-searched reference lists of relevant guidelines, reviews, and primary studies. We prioritized international guidance, systematic reviews, multicenter registries, prospective cohorts, and clinically informative mechanistic studies. Case reports and experimental studies were retained when they addressed questions not covered by higher-level evidence. The review was not protocol driven and did not include duplicate screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or a PRISMA flow diagram.Results
ICI-related cardiovascular toxicity extends beyond myocarditis to temporally associated atherosclerotic events, pericardial disease, and heart failure without demonstrable myocardial inflammation, although causal attribution is less secure for these non-myocarditis phenotypes. Current guidance supports baseline cardiovascular assessment and risk-adapted surveillance, but neither a universal troponin threshold nor an outcome-proven monitoring schedule has been established. Corticosteroids remain first-line treatment for clinically significant ICI myocarditis. Abatacept, ruxolitinib, alemtuzumab, and other intensified regimens are off-label and rest largely on nonrandomized or case-level evidence.Conclusion
Management should combine early recognition, careful exclusion of competing diagnoses, and coordinated oncology-cardiology decision-making. Current evidence does not justify uniform screening thresholds or a standard rescue regimen, and investigational biomarkers, imaging probes, and targeted immunomodulators require prospective validation.

La evidencia actual no justifica umbrales uniformes de detección o un régimen de rescate estándar, y los biomarcadores de investigación, sondas de imagen e inmunomoduladores específicos requieren validación prospectiva.

abstract_en:
Introduction
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention.Areas covered
This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications.Expert opinion
Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.

abstract_en: Postoperative pain management in otolaryngology requires balancing effective analgesia while minimizing adverse effects, such as opioid-related complications. Suzetrigine is a first-in-class selective voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV1.8) inhibitor that has been recently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. Suzetrigine selectively inhibits NaV1.8 channels expressed in peripheral nociceptive neurons, thereby reducing pain signaling without the respiratory depression, sedation, or misuse potential associated with opioids. This review summarizes the pharmacology, efficacy, safety profile, limitations, and potential applications of suzetrigine in otolaryngology. Prospective clinical trials consist of 2 phase 2 randomized clinical trials, 2 phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials, and 1 phase 3 open-label study involving more than 3000 patients. Across abdominoplasty and bunionectomy pain models, suzetrigine demonstrated superior analgesia compared with placebo and mixed efficacy comparable to hydrocodone/acetaminophen. The drug was generally well tolerated, with adverse event rates similar to placebo and no significant respiratory, cardiac, or sedating adverse effects reported. Additionally, 1 retrospective cohort study has reported results in patients undergoing free flap reconstruction and transoral robotic surgery. Suzetrigine is a promising nonopioid analgesic with demonstrated efficacy compared to placebo in acute postoperative pain and a favorable safety profile. In otolaryngology, suzetrigine may serve as an adjunct to multimodal analgesia and an opioid-sparing option for patients with contraindications to traditional analgesics, opioid use disorder, or procedures that are expected to have high opioid utilization such as tonsillectomy, sleep surgery, and major head and neck surgery. Future studies in otolaryngology are warranted to evaluate whether suzetrigine can meaningfully reduce postoperative opioid exposure without compromising analgesic effectiveness.

El manejo postoperatorio del dolor en otorrinolaringología requiere equilibrar la analgesia efectiva y minimizar los efectos adversos, como complicaciones relacionadas con los opioides. Suzetrigina es un inhibidor del canal de sodio de voltaje selectivo de primera clase (NaV1.8) que ha sido aprobado recientemente por la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de los Estados Unidos. Suzetrigina inhibe selectivamente los canales NaV1.8 expresados en neuronas nociceptivas periféricas, reduciendo así la señalización del dolor sin depresión respiratoria, sedación o potencial de mal uso asociado con los opioides. Los ensayos clínicos prospectivos constan de 2 ensayos clínicos aleatorizados de fase 2, 2 ensayos aleatorizados controlados con placebo en fase 3 y 1 ensayo abierto de fase 3 en el que participaron más de 3000 pacientes. En los modelos de dolor de abdominoplastia y junionectomía, la suzetrigina demostró analgesia superior en comparación con placebo y eficacia mixta comparable a hidrocodona/acetaminofén. El fármaco fue generalmente bien tolerado, con tasas de eventos adversos similares a placebo y sin efectos adversos respiratorios, cardíacos o sedantes significativos notificados. Además, 1 estudio retrospectivo de cohorte ha reportado resultados en pacientes sometidos a reconstrucción de colgajos libres y cirugía robótica transoral. La suzetrigina es un analgésico no opioides prometedor con eficacia demostrada en comparación con placebo en dolor postoperatorio agudo y un perfil de seguridad favorable. En otorrinolaringología, la suzetrigina puede servir como complemento a la analgesia multimodal y una opción ahorradora de opioides para pacientes con contraindicaciones a analgésicos tradicionales, trastorno por uso de opioides o procedimientos que se espera que tengan una alta utilización de opioides como la tonsilectomía, cirugía del sueño y cirugía mayor de cabeza y cuello.

abstract_en: Patients with advanced endometrial cancer (EC) have a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options after failure of prior systemic therapy. In this multi-cohort Phase II study (ETER200), patients with metastatic or recurrent EC who had received at least one chemotherapy regimen were enrolled. Based on MSI/MMR status, patients received benmelstobart plus anlotinib (Cohort 1), benmelstobart (Cohort 2), or anlotinib (Cohort 3) every 3 weeks. Primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1. Here, the results of Cohort 1 expansion stage were reported. As of May 9, 2024, 85 of the 107 non-MSI-H/pMMR EC patients enrolled in Cohort 1 constituted the expansion stage population for primary efficacy analysis. The IRC-assessed ORR was 34.1% (95% CI, 24.2-45.2), with a median duration of response of 15.2 months (95% CI, 6.9-not evaluable). Median progression-free and overall survival were 8.8 months (95% CI, 5.8-15.2) and 21.8 months (95% CI, 19.5-29.1), respectively. Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 69.2% of patients, most commonly hypertension (21.2%) and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome (9.4%). Overall, benmelstobart plus anlotinib showed promising anti-tumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in advanced non-MSI-H/pMMR EC, supporting further evaluation of this combination in randomized Phase III studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04574284.

abstract_en: Later-line therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) increasingly requires selection among treatments with different mechanisms, toxicity profiles, and sequencing evidence. Trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab has robust randomized evidence from SUNLIGHT, but objective response remains uncommon and hematologic toxicity can limit treatment delivery in heavily pretreated patients. Regorafenib and fruquintinib are minimally myelosuppressive oral alternatives, yet they differ in dose strategy, hepatotoxicity, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, and proteinuria. Accordingly, treatment selection should be individualized according to prior therapies, toxicity vulnerability, organ function, tumor tempo, and patient goals. Hypertension and proteinuria are important selection factors but may also be modifiable treatment-delivery factors. The proposed algorithms and adverse-event radar chart are intended as practical visual syntheses rather than validated guidelines or formal cross-trial comparisons.

La terapia de línea posterior para el cáncer colorrectal metastásico (CCRm) requiere cada vez más selección entre tratamientos con diferentes mecanismos, perfiles de toxicidad y evidencia de secuenciación. Trifluridina/tipiracilo más bevacizumab tiene evidencia aleatoria robusta de SUNLIGHT, pero la respuesta objetiva sigue siendo poco común y la toxicidad hematológica puede limitar la administración de tratamiento en pacientes fuertemente pretratados. Regorafenib y fruquintinib son alternativas orales mínimamente mielosupresoras, pero difieren en la estrategia de dosis, hepatotoxicidad, reacción cutánea mano-pie, hipertensión y proteinuria. Esta revisión narrativa actualiza evidencia pivotal y reciente y propone un marco informado de evidencia que trata la reserva hematológica como un constructo de aptitud clínica en lugar de un umbral de laboratorio fijo. Además, examinamos las implicaciones clínicas de bajas tasas de respuesta, exposición antiangiogénica previa, predictores moleculares emergentes incluyendo KRAS G12, evidencia en pacientes mayores o vulnerables, y desarrollos recientes en fase III. Los datos actuales no apoyan un biomarcador molecular validado para elegir entre estas tres opciones, y no existe una comparación aleatoria cabeza a cabeza de regorafenib y fruquintinib. En consecuencia, la selección del tratamiento debe ser individualizada según terapias previas, vulnerabilidad a la toxicidad, función orgánica, tempo tumoral y metas del paciente.La hipertensión y la proteinuria son factores de selección importantes, pero también pueden ser factores modificables de tratamiento-entrega.Los algoritmos propuestos y la tabla de radares de eventos adversos están destinados como síntesis visual práctica en lugar de directrices validadas o comparaciones formales entre los ensayos.

abstract_en: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined apolipoprotein B-containing lipoprotein independently associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and calcific aortic valve stenosis (CAVS). Circulating Lp(a) concentrations are largely inherited, minimally responsive to lifestyle modification, and not adequately addressed by conventional lipid-lowering pharmacotherapy. Patients with established ASCVD continue to experience recurrent cardiovascular events despite intensive guideline-directed therapy, and this residual risk reflects mechanisms - including persistently elevated Lp(a) - that are not captured by standard low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) management. In this narrative review, current evidence on Lp(a) biology, genetics, and pathophysiology is integrated with a critical appraisal of contemporary management, the emerging Lp(a)-lowering pharmacological landscape, and unresolved clinical implementation challenges. Current management relies on once-in-adulthood Lp(a) measurement for cardiovascular risk stratification, aggressive optimization of modifiable risk factors, and, in highly selected patients, lipoprotein apheresis; no Lp(a)-specific pharmacotherapy is approved by any major regulatory agency. RNA-targeted therapies - antisense oligonucleotides and small interfering RNA agents - and an oral inhibitor of Lp(a) particle assembly have produced pharmacodynamic Lp(a) reductions of 80-95% or more in phase 2 randomized trials. However, topline results from the phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial showed that pelacarsen, despite lowering Lp(a), did not reduce the primary composite cardiovascular endpoint. Full trial data are awaited, while four other phase 3 cardiovascular outcome trials - OCEAN(a)-Outcomes, ACCLAIM-Lp(a), MOVE-Lp(a), and OCEAN(a)-PreEvent - remain ongoing. Should positive outcome data emerge, clinical implementation will require regulatory approval, evidence-based patient selection, standardized treatment thresholds, and equitable access strategies across diverse populations.

Las concentraciones de Lp(a) circulantes son en gran parte hereditarias, mínimamente sensibles a la modificación del estilo de vida, y no son tratadas adecuadamente por la farmacoterapia convencional hipolipemiante. Los pacientes con ASCVD establecidos continúan experimentando eventos cardiovasculares recurrentes a pesar de la terapia intensiva dirigida por directrices, y este riesgo residual refleja mecanismos - incluyendo Lp(a) persistentemente elevados - que no son capturados por el manejo estándar de colesterol lipoproteínas de baja densidad (LDL-C). En esta revisión narrativa, la evidencia actual sobre la Lp(a) biología, genética y fisiopatología se integra con una evaluación crítica del manejo contemporáneo, el emergente panorama farmacológico de Lp(a) disminución y los desafíos de implementación clínica no resueltos.El manejo actual se basa en la medición de Lp(a) una vez en la edad adulta para estratificación del riesgo cardiovascular, optimización agresiva de factores de riesgo modificables y, en pacientes altamente seleccionados, aféresis de lipoproteínas; ninguna farmacoterapia específica de Lp(a) es aprobada por cualquier agencia reguladora importante. Las terapias dirigidas al ARN - oligonucleótidos antisensibles y pequeños agentes de ARN interferentes - y un inhibidor oral del ensamblaje de partículas Lp(a) han producido reducciones de Lp(a) farmacodinámicas de 80-95% o más en ensayos aleatorizados de fase 2. Sin embargo, los resultados de primera línea del ensayo de fase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON mostraron que pelacarsen, a pesar de disminuir Lp(a), no redujo la variable cardiovascular compuesta primaria. Se esperan datos completos del ensayo, mientras que otros cuatro ensayos de resultado cardiovascular en fase 3 - OCEAN(a)-Outcomes, ACCLAM-Lp(a), MOVE-Lp(a) y OCEAN(a)-PreEvento - permanecen en curso. Si surgen datos de resultados positivos, la implementación clínica requerirá aprobación reglamentaria, selección de pacientes basada en evidencia, umbrales de tratamiento estandarizados y estrategias de acceso equitativo en diversas poblaciones.

abstract_en:
Background
Coronary heart disease (CHD) is among the more common cardiovascular diseases, affecting 4.7 million people in Germany alone. As many as 20% of patients with CHD still suffer from angina pectoris despite appropriate antianginal therapy and revascularization. Refractory angina pectoris reduces quality of life and increases mortality. In this review, we describe therapeutic strategies and the clinical evidence underlying them.Methods
This review is based on publications up to December 2025 retrieved through a selective search in Medline/PubMed for RCTs, before-and-after studies, and guidelines on the treatment of refractory angina pectoris.Results
The treatment of refractory angina pectoris begins with reducing risk factors, optimizing pharmacotherapy, and considering revascularization for functionally significant coronary stenosis. If these treatment options have been exhausted, the implantation of a sinus reducer may be considered, as recommended in the European guidelines (recommendation grade IIb). The evidence for this is derived from randomized trials and from multiple registry and observational studies. In the sham-controlled COSIRA trial, which involved 104 patients, an improvement in angina symptoms by at least two classes on the Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) grading scale was observed in 35% of patients six months after implantation, compared with 15% in the control group. The multicenter ORBITA-COSMIC trial, which involved 51 patients, also yielded a reduction in daily angina pectoris compared with the control group (OR 1.40; 95% CI: [1.08; 1.83]). Potential complications include migration, embolization of the reducer, and coronary sinus perforation or dissection in 1-2% of patients. These events are only rarely clinically significant.Conclusion
The sinus reducer may improve symptoms in selected patients, but the reported periprocedural complications and limited evidence to date on long-term outcomes should enter into the decision whether to provide this treatment to the individual patient.

abstract_en: In recent years, with the considerable changes in the therapeutic armamentarium for diabetes, the incidence of hypoglycemia events, especially severe hypoglycemia events, associated with drug treatment in people with diabetes has markedly decreased. We were prompted to evaluate the threshold for each intervention target, especially glycemic control, associated with a minimized risk of the macrovascular complications of diabetes in this setting. In the Japan Diabetes Optimal Integrated Treatment study for 3 major risk factors of cardiovascular diseases (J-DOIT3) conducted by us previously, we recruited 2542 participants and assigned them to a conventional therapy group (n = 1271) and an intensive therapy group (n = 1271; two ineligible participants were removed from all analyses afterwards), and the incidence of severe hypoglycemia events was low in both groups (7 in the intensive therapy group and 4 in the conventional therapy group during a median 8.5 years' follow-up). Towards the objective of this study, we undertook a landmark analysis with a landmark time-point of 1 year after the baseline of the J-DOIT3 study. Then, using the updated mean values of the glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), systolic blood pressure, and LDL-cholesterol and HDL-cholesterol levels, we determined the optimal levels of each of these variables associated with the lowest hazard ratios for outcomes, including the primary and cardiovascular outcomes. For glycemic control, our results revealed no clear lower threshold of the glycated hemoglobin associated with the lowest risk of myocardial infarction or all-cause mortality; for other risk factors, it might be an important treatment target to maintain the LDL-cholesterol levels at below 80 mg/dL to minimize the risk of stroke. The present analysis suggested that the treatment target for HbA1c to minimize the risk of all-cause mortality in participants with diabetes with a low incidence of severe hypoglycemia episodes could be < 6.5% (ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00300976).
abstract_es: Abstract

En los últimos años, con los considerables cambios en el armamento terapéutico para la diabetes, la incidencia de eventos de hipoglucemia, especialmente eventos de hipoglucemia grave, asociados con el tratamiento farmacológico en personas con diabetes ha disminuido notablemente. Se nos pidió evaluar el umbral para cada objetivo de intervención, especialmente control glucémico, asociado con un riesgo minimizado de complicaciones macrovasculares de la diabetes en este entorno. En el estudio Japan Diabetes Optimal Integrated Treatment para 3 principales factores de riesgo de enfermedades cardiovasculares (J-DOIT3) realizado por nosotros anteriormente, reclutamos a 2542 participantes y los asignamos a un grupo de terapia convencional (n = 1271) y a un grupo de terapia intensiva (n = 1271; dos participantes no elegibles fueron retirados de todos los análisis posteriores), y la incidencia de eventos de hipoglucemia grave fue baja en ambos grupos (7 en el grupo de terapia intensiva y 4 en el grupo de terapia convencional durante una mediana de 8,5 años de seguimiento). Hacia el objetivo de este estudio, realizamos un análisis de hito con un punto de referencia de 1 año después del inicio del estudio J-DOIT3. Luego, utilizando los valores medios actualizados de la hemoglobina glucatada (HbA1c), la presión arterial sistólica y los niveles de colesterol LDL y colesterol HDL, determinamos los niveles óptimos de cada una de estas variables asociadas con los índices de riesgo más bajos para los resultados, incluyendo los resultados primarios y cardiovasculares.Para el control glucémico, nuestros resultados no revelaron un umbral claramente inferior de la hemoglobina glucatada asociada con el menor riesgo de infarto de miocardio o mortalidad por cualquier causa; para otros factores de riesgo, podría ser un importante objetivo de tratamiento mantener los niveles de colesterol LDL por debajo de 80 mg/dL para minimizar el riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular. El presente análisis sugiere que el objetivo de tratamiento de la HbA1c para minimizar el riesgo de mortalidad por cualquier causa en participantes con diabetes con baja incidencia de episodios de hipoglucemia grave podría ser < 6,5% (ClinicalTrials.gov, número NCT00300976).

abstract_en: Background Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, resulting in an increasing demand for long-term treatment options for patients with end-stage heart failure. While heart transplantation is the gold standard, donor organ shortage continues to be a major limitation, particularly in countries with opt-in consent systems. Summary Durable mechanical circulatory support (dMCS) devices have emerged as a critical therapy for patients with advanced heart failure, either as a bridge to transplantation or as destination therapy. Technological innovations over recent decades have transitioned from pulsatile to continuous-flow systems, with the HeartMate 3 currently representing the only long-term left ventricular support, due to its superior hemocompatibility, clinical outcomes, and full magnetic levitation. However, limitations persist, especially regarding right-sided and biventricular support, driveline infections, and patient quality of life. This review provides a comprehensive overview of both currently approved and investigational dMCS devices, highlighting key engineering features, hemocompatibility advancements, and the status of ongoing clinical trials. Emerging devices such as the Corheart 6, BrioVAD, EvaHeart 2, CorWave, FlowMaker, and TorVAD aim to enhance physiologic support, minimize shear stress, and enable full implantability. Additionally, novel concepts for biventricular and total heart replacement, including BerlinHeart Excor, reBEAT, DuoCor BiVAS, SynCardia, Emperor and BiVACOR are discussed. Key Messages •HeartMate 3 remains the only approved LVAD in Europe following HVAD withdrawal. •Next-generation devices aim to improve hemocompatibility, reduce complications, and support full implantability. •Options for biventricular or right heart failure remain limited, but novel concepts are emerging.

Antecedentes Las enfermedades cardiovasculares siguen siendo la principal causa de muerte en todo el mundo, lo que da lugar a una creciente demanda de opciones de tratamiento a largo plazo para los pacientes con insuficiencia cardiaca terminal. Si bien el trasplante de corazón es el patrón oro, la escasez de órganos donantes sigue siendo una limitación importante, especialmente en los países con sistemas de consentimiento opt-in. Las innovaciones tecnológicas en las últimas décadas han pasado de sistemas pulsatiles a sistemas de flujo continuo, con el HeartMate 3 representando actualmente el único soporte ventricular izquierdo a largo plazo, debido a su superior hemocompatibilidad, resultados clínicos y levitación magnética completa. Sin embargo, persisten limitaciones, especialmente en lo que respecta al soporte derecho y biventricular, las infecciones de la línea motriz y la calidad de vida del paciente. Esta revisión proporciona una visión completa de los dispositivos dMCS actualmente aprobados y de investigación, destacando características clave de ingeniería, avances en la hemocompatibilidad y el estado de los ensayos clínicos en curso. Los dispositivos emergentes como Corheart 6, BrioVAD, EvaHeart 2, CorWave, FlowMaker y TorVAD tienen como objetivo mejorar el soporte fisiológico, minimizar el estrés de corte y permitir la implantación completa.Además, se discuten nuevos conceptos para el reemplazo biventricular y total del corazón, incluyendo BerlinHeart Excor, reBEAT, DuoCor BIVAS, SynCardia, Emperor y BiVACOR. Mensajes clave •HeartMate 3 sigue siendo el único LVAD aprobado en Europa después de la retirada del HVAD. •Los dispositivos de próxima generación tienen como objetivo mejorar la hemocompatibilidad, reducir complicaciones y apoyar la implantabilidad completa. •Las opciones para la insuficiencia cardíaca biventricular o derecha siguen siendo limitadas, pero están surgiendo nuevos conceptos.
